subject: Urgent: OMEGA2C tail-latency spike — request for temporary SLO exemption and rollback contingency

Subject: Sudden tail latency increasing errors for /stream endpoint (model: OMEGA2C v2)

Hi Hannah,

We started seeing elevated tail latency (99th) against the /stream inference endpoint for OMEGA2C v2 around 08:50 PDT this morning. Our customer-facing widgets are timing out and retrying, and we're seeing a ~3% error rate for requests that previously were sub-0.2%. The same traffic routed to your v2 fallback (OMEGA2C-quant) has lower latency but different output in a few cases.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is a runtime regression in v2 that would justify reverting traffic to the previous stable variant? We have an upcoming merchant payroll run at 11:00 and need to know if we should fail over to the quant variant proactively or expect a short-lived blip.

I'm attaching a short sample log and a screenshot of our dashboard.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Platform — SequoiaPay

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the samples. We see the same alert firing in our monitoring: ALERT-7342 (OMEGA2C v2, p99 jump).

Quick status: engineering is investigating trace-level logs now. Initial look shows higher attention kernel contention on some GPU shapes around longer contexts (>= 1024 tokens). Rishi, can you confirm whether the kernel rollout from last week's deploy could explain the p99 behavior?

Options to propose to the customer now:
- Temporary SLO exemption (limit window to 4 hours) while we stabilize; Redwood would accept a reduced SLO for the period in exchange for not routing back to the older variant.
- Controlled traffic rollback to OMEGA2C v1-stable or to the quant variant (both are compatible but have subtle output differences).

Elena, I want to align on the operational impact for SequoiaPay if we do a short rollback vs granting an exception. If you want a full rollback, we will need an explicit sign-off from contact in your ops team and Redwood leadership approval for an overnight rollback.

I'm attaching our rollback playbook excerpt and a current p99 snapshot.

— Hannah

Subject: Re: Sudden tail latency increasing errors for /stream endpoint (model: OMEGA2C v2)

Quick summary from infra: the deploy at 03:10 UTC introduced a kernel selector tweak for longer attention windows that improves average throughput but in rare scheduling paths increases GC-like stalls on our multi-tenant scheduler. We currently see the p99 spike correlated with requests that hit both long context + self-attention caching misses.

Mitigations being executed (in parallel):
1) Hotfix to scheduler to lower max-concurrent-long-context per-worker (rolling restart underway; expected to finish by 11:10 PDT).
2) Temporary traffic cap on merchants with > 1k token contexts.
3) If the above does not reduce p99 to within 20% of target by 12:00 PDT, recommend rollback to OMEGA2C v1-stable for affected customer route.

If we do rollback, note: model parameterization differs and a small delta in grounding may surface (we should surface a QA note). Also requires a traffic migration window of ~6 minutes with graceful drain.

Rishi
Senior Staff SW Eng, Serving Runtime

Elena — which would you prefer? Sohould we proceed with Option A as a precaution?

Soojin, Hannah — please coordinate the customer notice and technically schedule the migration. Rishi — execute the rollback playbook and confirm completion.
